title: Landlords face £5,000 compliance costs under new act
summary:
Landlords have incurred median costs of £5,000 in complying with the Renters' Rights Act, according to a survey of approximately 200 property investors conducted by Handelsbanken. The figure exceeds earlier government estimates for compliance costs under the legislation.

title: First-time buyer demand falls as stock shortage persists
summary:
First-time buyer demand across Britain fell to 32.9% in Q2 2026, down from 34.8% in the previous quarter, according to Yopa research. Stock shortages persist, with first-time buyer suitable properties accounting for just 1.7% of all homes listed for sale.

title: Energy efficiency important to buyers but few willing to pay premium
summary:
Energy efficiency ranks as a priority for 85% of homebuyers, but only 2% would pay significantly more for better-performing properties, according to LRG's survey of over 700 buyers and sellers. The research indicates buyers focus on running costs rather than energy ratings, with 36% willing to pay more only if offset by lower bills.

title: Lender completes £2.4m refinance on 55-unit block
summary:
Specialist lender Rely has completed a £2.4 million multi-unit freehold block remortgage for a portfolio landlord in Northumberland, secured against a 55-unit residential property valued at £3.2 million. The transaction involved refinancing a fully refurbished residential block held on a single freehold title.

title: Paragon provides £8.8m for 51-home Preston development
summary:
Paragon Development Finance has provided an £8.8 million facility to Oakwood Group for a 51-home residential development in Broughton, near Preston. The funding covers site acquisition at Garstang Road and construction of the scheme, which includes 20 affordable housing units.

The post Paragon provides £8.8m for 51-home Preston development appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Property tax reform divides UK regions, survey finds
summary:
A survey of 2,203 UK adults has revealed significant regional differences in attitudes towards replacing council tax and stamp duty with an annual property tax. Support was strongest in northern England and Wales at 35-37%, while opposition was highest in London and the South East at 23-28%, with 37% of respondents nationally remaining undecided.

title: 76% of landlords plan refinancing to expand portfolios
summary:
More than three-quarters of buy-to-let landlords intend to refinance their property portfolios within the next year to fund additional acquisitions, according to research from specialist lender Together. The survey revealed that 76% of landlords are likely to refinance in the next 12 months, with investment activity shifting towards northern England and Scotland.

title: Viability challenges threaten housing targets, warns Colliers
summary:
Planning reform will not be sufficient to meet government housebuilding targets unless ministers address viability challenges facing developers, according to property consultancy Colliers. Andrew White, head of UK residential at Colliers, has warned that the economics of residential development have changed significantly.

title: UK house price growth slows to 2.7% in May 2026
summary:
House price growth in the UK decelerated in May 2026, with annual growth slowing to 2.7% from 3.9% the previous month. Regional variations remain significant, with Northern Ireland leading at 7.4% annual growth while London prices fell 3.7%.

The post UK house price growth slows to 2.7% in May 2026 appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: UK inflation falls to 2.6% but housing affordability concerns persist
summary:
UK inflation fell to 2.6% in June 2026, matching a 15-month low, according to ONS data. However, property industry experts warn household affordability remains under pressure, with the decline potentially temporary as higher energy costs are expected to push inflation higher in coming months.
